title: AuthorityIdentity
description: The cross-repo identity of one authority/judgment - which citable case this is, independent of good-law status (see good-law-status.schema.json / citator-finding.schema.json for that) and independent of AI-service-internal ranking/display fields (authority_weight, headnote_id, full_text_ref, is_canary) that stay local to services/ai. Derived from jura-app's services/ai/src/juraai_ai/corpus/models.py::CanonicalAuthority (read in full 2026-07-27), scoped to the identity-defining subset load-bearing in corpus/repository.py's CorpusIntegrityError: `id` is the PRIMARY KEY over the whole corpus (Doc 16 §1) - a duplicate id is a data-integrity violation the repository fails fast on, never a silent last-write-wins, because the citation index and get_authority() must never disagree about which object an id names. `neutral_citation` is Jura's own IP layer and is UNIQUE (Doc 16 §1). This schema is the identity concept only; the Postgres-backed corpus (Phase 5) and jura-data's own judgment/citation tables are mapped against it in Phase 5.1's data-contract-alignment step, not decided here. Phase 3.3.2 of the Jura AI engineering foundation plan.

id.description: The PRIMARY KEY identifying exactly one authority across the whole corpus (visible and canary rows share one id space). A duplicate id is a data-integrity violation (CorpusIntegrityError), not an ambiguity to resolve around.

neutral_citation.description: Jura's own neutral-citation IP layer (see neutral-citation.schema.json for the parsed form) - UNIQUE per authority (Doc 16 §1).

reported_citations.description: Raw reported-citation strings for this authority (e.g. "PLD 2019 SC 675"). Matches CanonicalAuthority.reported_citations exactly: a tuple of raw strings, not pre-normalized - see reported-citation.schema.json for the normalization step callers apply.

parties.description: The party-name string (e.g. "Khan v. Federal Board of Revenue"), used both for display and as the bounded-fuzzy-resolution candidate key (Doc 16 §2).

court.description: The court that decided this authority (expanded form, e.g. "Supreme Court" - see normalize_court in verifier/normalize.py for the abbreviation-expansion rule).

court_level.description: Court-level rank on Jura's court-hierarchy scale (Doc 24 §11): 1=District, 2=Tribunal, 3=High Court, 4=Federal Shariat, 5=Supreme. Kept as a plain integer (not a closed enum) so an out-of-range or future rank from the corpus does not fail to parse - the corpus is the source of truth, consumers degrade rather than throw.

jurisdiction.description: The jurisdiction this authority belongs to (e.g. "PK") - load-bearing for the good-law engine, which models Pakistani edges only (see GoodLawStatus.untracked's meaning for a foreign authority).

date.description: The decision date, when known. Optional: some corpus rows genuinely lack a confirmed date.
